author: 0xBaqi
text:
what if you could research a token without knowing what happened next?

that’s the idea behind Parallax, my submission for the @nansen_ai Meridian Buildathon.

crypto research has a hindsight problem.

once a token pumps, crashes, or becomes a huge story, it’s easy to look back at old onchain data and convince ourselves the outcome was obvious.

Parallax removes that advantage.

choose a token and a historical cutoff. Parallax uses Nansen’s historical data to reconstruct what was actually knowable at that moment, participant flows, smart money movement, price context and evidence coverage.

everything after the cutoff is sealed behind a temporal firewall.

you see the evidence.
you make your decision.
you lock it.

only then do you get to see what happened next.

if historical data is missing, Parallax keeps it unavailable instead of silently turning missing evidence into a signal.

Time Machine lets you revisit curated historical moments without hindsight.

Investigate lets you reconstruct your own moments across Ethereum and Solana, with deterministic evidence receipts and Nansen provenance.

no buy/sell calls. no prediction score.

evidence, not prediction.

 live: https://t.co/u0nuIMHCvy

github: https://t.co/mfUt7HYnxw

the future changes how the past looks.

author: Iziedking
text:
For the @nansen_ai Meridian Buildathon, I built NOCK.

2026 has been brutal for on-chain money.

April 1: Drift on Solana lost $285M in 12 minutes.

April 18: Attackers drained $292M of rsETH from Kelp’s bridge, used it as collateral on Aave and borrowed roughly $190M in ETH.

Aave itself wasn’t hacked yet $8.45B left the protocol within 48 hours and DeFi TVL dropped $13B in two days.

September 24: Bitget lost $351.6M from its hot wallets and paused withdrawals.

The exploit takes minutes but damage can spread for hours and leave a devastating impact

I built NOCK for those hours.

NOCK watches the vaults, yield dollars, and lending markets where people park capital across Ethereum, Arc and Robinhood Chain using live @nansen_ai data.

Instead of using one generic threshold, NOCK measures every venue against its own normal behavior.

When wallets start leaving unusually fast NOCK detects a run.

When suspicious or stolen collateral starts spreading into lending markets, NOCK detects contagion.

We replayed the Kelp incident using Nansen data.

NOCK’s contagion alarm fired at 17:42 UTC 78 minutes before major WETH lenders rushed to exit.

On Stream xUSD the run alarm fired 7 days before withdrawals froze.

But detecting risk isn’t enough.

NOCK can act.

You place your deposit behind a small guard contract controlled by your wallet.

If NOCK raises an alarm on that vault, a keeper can call exit() and return the funds directly to your wallet.

That is the only action the keeper is allowed to perform.

I tested the full flow on Arc testnet:

Deposit → drill → alarm → exit → funds back home → Telegram transaction alert.

NOCK also adds a safety layer for copy trading.

Before copying a wallet, you can see who entered first and whether early wallets sold into the traders who followed.

This week on Solana, NOCK identified 25 early wallets selling into buyers who arrived after a smart trader’s entry.

And agents can use all of this too.

Add the NOCK MCP to Claude Code or Codex.

Once the free credits are exhausted, agents can pay $0.02 per call in USDC on Arc via x402.

author: blackpoint_team
text:
⚒️I built an experimental market intelligence module for the Nansen Meridian Buildathon - now integrated into the beta version of OTG Analytics.

Link: https://t.co/Wxv1dSLPwQ

OTG Analytics is an analytics platform I'm building for the @playoffthegrid NFT market on OpenSea.

For the Meridian Buildathon, I wanted to test a question that couldn't be answered by looking at the NFT market alone:
Is there a measurable relationship between $GUN market activity and what happens in the Off The Grid NFT market on OpenSea?

The new module combines Nansen data with more than a year of historical OTG marketplace data.

It tracks $GUN market conditions and compares major positive and negative $GUN price movements with subsequent changes in:
• OTG NFT transactions
• NFT trading volume in GUN
• unique OTG NFT buyers

Instead of comparing two charts visually, the system identifies historically unusual $GUN price movements and measures how the OTG NFT market behaved at 0h, 1h, 6h and 24h around those events.

For every horizon it shows the median historical reaction, number of comparable events and the middle 50% of observed outcomes.

The final dataset contained 145 independent positive $GUN shocks and 145 negative shocks.

And the result was interesting precisely because it wasn't a clean signal:
the historical relationship between $GUN price movements and OTG NFT activity on OpenSea was weak and inconsistent.

Transactions, volume and buyer participation behaved differently across time horizons, while similar $GUN movements often resulted in very different NFT market outcomes.

So the module doesn't manufacture a trading signal from noisy data.

Instead, it turns Nansen data into historical market context - showing what happened in the OTG NFT market after comparable $GUN events before, how large those reactions were, and how consistent they actually were.

No strong relationship is still a result.

That's what I wanted this experiment to do: test an assumption with data rather than assume the relationship exists.

Built with the Nansen API for the @nansen_ai Meridian Buildathon, and integrated directly into the beta version of OTG Analytics.

The experiment ended up being more API-intensive than I initially expected — the first Nansen API allocation wasn't enough to complete the development and validation, so I had to continue with a second API key.

That included testing the data pipeline, building the historical dataset, validating the integration and running the live component now connected to OTG Analytics.

author: cifreXnet
text:
Built Polygraph on the @nansen_ai API for the Meridian Buildathon — an onchain lie detector.

Prediction markets show what capital SAYS. Nansen flow intelligence shows what it DOES. I put them on one instrument.

Eight needles: the Polymarket crowd on top, then six real cohorts of onchain capital — top-PnL wallets, smart money, whales, exchanges, fresh wallets. When the crowd's needle and the smart money's needle point opposite ways, the band between them goes red.

Then the part I couldn't skip: is the crowd even worth fading? Every Polymarket binary settles at $1 or $0, so I scored 900 resolved markets against their own settlement. 3,580 observations.

The crowd is well calibrated. Brier 0.08.

Which makes divergence more interesting, not less — when a calibrated crowd and the best wallets onchain disagree, someone informed is wrong.

1,219 API calls. All live.

Repo: https://t.co/sx4oEAAKoV
Live: https://t.co/6sSwBDtbm1

author: orvynel
text:
Nansen team — thank you for Meridian, and for opening Token God Mode to build on. A short note to go with my demo.

The video is just a highlight. Crucible has more depth than I could fit into a short clip without rushing, so I kept it tight and would rather you experience the rest hands-on. Everything is live and open source.

What Crucible is: an honest backtester for Nansen Smart Money. Compose a signal in plain English — pick a cohort, say what they're doing, choose a hold — and it replays across 990 point-in-time scenarios with no look-ahead, telling you whether following the smart money actually beat just holding.

What's on the site, beyond the clip:

• The equity curve & "If you invested $X": Watch the strategy grow chronologically. Type any amount to see your real-dollar outcome, so you can see the data is real and moving, not a mockup.

• Fully composable rules: Stack conditions (AND/OR), set net-buy/sell thresholds across 6 cohorts and 5 holding horizons.

• Honest metrics: Hit rate and median lead the verdict — both robust to outliers by design. The averages and equity curve are winsorized so one lucky meme coin can't fake an edge, and max drawdown is shown too.

• Full receipts: Open any trade to see the forward return and the cohort flows behind the move — and, on most, the actual Nansen wallets, labels, and dollar amounts. You can check, trade by trade, that the numbers are real.

• Live Nansen explorer: Run real queries against Nansen right in the app — the same endpoints Crucible is built on. Open source and unit-tested.

Try it live: https://t.co/Qx63Jpr9At
Read the code: https://t.co/gzsM4XrN1D

Please open it and push on it — compose a signal, watch the curve, open the receipts, and run a live query. Thank you for building the data that made this possible.

— Orvynel

author: tot_crypto
text:
A lot of people still don't know that Nansen is more than an onchain analytics tool right now, Nansen offers trading, spot and perp directly through their wallet, you can stake your tokens with them, you also get to make predictions as well.

Ok so, as a little Nansen fan, I was looking for ways to make money through the platform😄 and it occured to me that I can trade perps on there, but the thing is I don't want to manually analyse tokens myself and place trades myself and besides I trade a lot based on my emotions so why not automate this process entirely and see how it goes. 

So I created an autonomous trading bot and this also happens to align with the Nansen Meridian Buildathon week so I guess this is my entry for it. The bot selects tokens to trade for me based on Smart Money Net Accumulation, combines Nansen's Hyperliquid perp positioning data with real on-chain spot exchange/whale/smart-trader net flow for the same token, execute the trade, take profit and stop loss when necessary. I left the core decision to whether buy, sell or hold to LLMs integrated in the bot. 8 agents debate every trade using the data from Nansen: on-chain, sentiment, technical, macro and fundamentals feed a bull vs bear debate, then a trader, a risk manager and a portfolio manager handles the rest. 

All the onchain analysis and trade execution run through Nansen API plus I get to earn Nansen points for all my trades😉 which may become very useful in the future.

Bonus: I created a meeting room where I can view my agents as they debate and execute trades in real time, fun to watch

Give it a try
